Install opencode on Omarchy

Opencode is an MIT-licensed, open-source coding agent centered on a rich terminal UI: you chat with it, it reads and edits files in your project, and runs commands on your behalf, with separate build (full-access) and plan (read-only) modes. A desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux is now available in beta on top of the same agent. You bring your own API key from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google or any of 75+ supported providers.

Watch: OpenCode CRASH Course | OPEN SOURCE AI CODING AGENT ↗

  1. Open a terminal.
  2. Run the install command:
    omarchy pkg add opencode
  3. Check it landed. Pacman should list version 1.1.51-1:
    pacman -Qi opencode

Open and use opencode

opencode is a desktop app. Press Super + Space to open the launcher and search for it. If it does not show up by name, list the desktop entries the package installed:

pacman -Ql opencode | grep applications

opencode requirements and compatibility

  • An API key from a supported LLM provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, etc.) or a free/local model
  • Network access to the chosen provider

Dependencies Omarchy installs for you

  • curl
  • gcc-libs
  • glibc
  • icu
  • ripgrep
  • tar

Free and open source (The tool itself is free and open source; you pay your chosen LLM provider for API usage). License: MIT.

Frequently asked questions

How do I install opencode on Omarchy?

Open a terminal and run omarchy pkg add opencode. The download is 24.1 MB and it takes 107.8 MB once installed. Omarchy pulls in any dependencies automatically.

Is opencode free?

Free and open source (The tool itself is free and open source; you pay your chosen LLM provider for API usage). The package is licensed MIT.

How do I uninstall opencode?

Run omarchy pkg drop opencode. It removes the package from your system.

What does opencode depend on?

The package declares 6 dependencies: curl, gcc-libs, glibc, icu, ripgrep, tar. Omarchy installs them for you.

Is opencode a desktop app?

Yes. Open the launcher with Super + Space and search for opencode.

Is opencode in the official Omarchy repo?

Yes. It is published as opencode (version 1.1.51-1) in the official Omarchy package repository. Anomaly makes it. Project site: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode. This site is unofficial and not affiliated with Omarchy or Omacom.
